analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation line in docs/developer/test.md (base/head line 918). It now says Flint is paged-only, so DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND may only be unset or `paged`. The earlier text said the variable selects `contiguous` or `paged`. The patch touches no source, protocol, crypto, attestation, authorization or build/release logic, so no runtime control or trust boundary changes.

I checked the change against the relevant threat model material. T-041 (prefix-cache and SSD tier, TB-007) is the closest match, because the document discusses FlintLiveTests with a task-local encrypted-cache directory and isolated test roots. The edit does not touch the cache policy, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, the KEK, the disk budget or the cache-storage validation.

The edit also does not weaken the test isolation guidance. It does not add a way to point tests at production state, or any new environment variable or secret, and the guidance about not using production cache roots or keys is unchanged.

One open question for integration: the statement that Flint is paged-only rests on code outside this diff. I cannot confirm that DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND=contiguous is now rejected, or that the surrounding doc lines, such as the 'DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND=paged' instructions near lines 875-889, stay consistent with it. Any mismatch there is a documentation accuracy issue, not a security regression.

No findings.
